[1, 2, 7] Key provisions of the bill include prohibiting the use of cash transfers, food vouchers, and food procured internationally. [1, 2] It also mandates that at least 50% of the program's annual funding be used for the procurement and ocean transportation of American agricultural products, while reducing the allowable percentage for administrative expenses. [2, 3] The rebound in rice acres was attributed to higher prices for the commodity. This period of price stability occurred while the global rice market was significantly impacted by India's decision to ban the export of non-basmati white rice in July 2023. India, the world's largest rice exporter, accounted for approximately 40% of the global rice trade in the 2022-2023 marketing year, and the ban affected about 15% of global rice trade. <3> In a report published on September 19, 2023, the USDA analyzed the global impact of India's rice export restrictions, which were projected to cause a decline in global rice trade for both 2023 and 2024. [6] India, the world's largest rice exporter, initiated these disruptions by banning non-basmati white rice exports on July 20, 2023, and subsequently imposing an export tax on parboiled rice in August 2023. [4, 6] These actions triggered a surge in global rice prices to their highest levels since 2008, as importers shifted demand to the next largest suppliers, Thailand and Vietnam. [2] The USDA report noted that U.S. rice exports were not expected to be significantly affected, as their prices were already substantially higher than the global average. [2] <4> On July 20, 2023, India, the world's largest rice exporter, announced an immediate ban on the export of non-basmati white rice. The measure, implemented by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade, was intended to control rising domestic prices and ensure domestic food security amid concerns of a potentially poor monsoon. This action, which amended the export policy for this rice category from "free" to "prohibited," immediately sparked concerns about the stability of global rice supplies and prices. <5> On June 28, 2023, Anheuser-Busch, the leading end-user of rice in the United States, launched a new advertising campaign titled "We Make the Beer" to coincide with the start of the summer season. The campaign's purpose is to recognize the various components of its business, including employees, branding, partnerships, and programming that contribute to their product. Featured in the campaign is Eric Vaught, a fourth-generation rice farmer from Hickory Ridge, Arkansas, who represents the many American farmers who supply the critical rice ingredient for the company's brewing process. This initiative underscores the significant role of the U.S. rice industry in Anheuser-Busch's products and the nation's economy. <6> A bipartisan group of U.S. Representatives, including Tracey Mann (R-KS), John Garamendi (D-CA), Rick Crawford (R-AR), and Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), introduced H.R. 4293, the 'American Farmers Feed the World Act of 2023'. [1, 2, 7] Key provisions of the bill include prohibiting the use of cash transfers, food vouchers, and food procured internationally. [1, 2] It also mandates that at least 50% of the program's annual funding be used for the procurement and ocean transportation of American agricultural products, while reducing the allowable percentage for administrative expenses. [1, 9] The bill proposes to increase oversight for the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) by requiring more detailed reporting to Congress and transferring some authorities to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). [1, 3, 7] The proposed legislation has garnered support from over 55 agricultural and maritime organizations. The warm and wet weather conditions created a favorable environment for fungal diseases such as blast and cercospora, prompting growers to actively scout their fields. While some disease was beginning to appear, LSU AgCenter entomologist Blake Wilson reported that insect pressure had been minimal so far in the growing season. <8> The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced the Rice Production Program (RPP) on May 5, 2023, to provide financial assistance to rice producers impacted by stagnant prices and high input costs during the 2022 crop year. The program, funded with up to $250 million from the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023, was administered by the Farm Service Agency (FSA). The FSA began mailing pre-filled applications to eligible producers during the week of May 8, 2023. The deadline for producers to sign and return the completed applications to their local FSA office was Monday, July 10, 2023. Following the application period, an initial payment was issued, and a final payment was announced on September 22, 2023, to be paid out by the end of that month. <9> On May 2, 2023, the California Rice Commission announced the commencement of its surface water monitoring programs for the 2023 rice growing season. [3] The Rice Pesticide Program (RPP) was scheduled to begin on May 9, 2023. [3] Monitoring for the Waste Discharge Requirements (WDR) and the Pyrethroid Pesticides Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) was set to start the following week. [3] These monitoring initiatives are crucial for ensuring regulatory compliance with the Central Valley Water Board and for assessing the effectiveness of the industry's management practices. [3] <10> In an initial progress report on the 2023 U.S. rice planting season published on April 21, 2023, USA Rice detailed varied progress across the country. Planting was substantially finished along the Gulf Coast of Texas and Louisiana. In Texas, conventional rice planting was mostly complete, with the crop reported to be in good condition, though recent showers had slowed progress in areas east of Houston. Southwest Louisiana had also largely completed planting, but faced challenges with pests and seedling diseases. In the mid-South, states like Arkansas, Mississippi, and Missouri were experiencing normal planting progress. Arkansas was estimated to be 40% planted, while Mississippi stood at about 25% complete. Missouri's planting progress was reported to be between 40-50% complete. Fieldwork was just beginning in California, where recent rains had caused some delays to land preparation.

metadata.original_text: This time series records rice USD cwt data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2024-08-26 to 2024-09-11. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The potential for a large U.S. rice crop was questioned following extreme rains from Hurricane Beryl, which made landfall in Texas on July 8, 2024. The storm particularly impacted southern growing areas near Houston, including Wharton, Brazoria, Matagorda, Colorado, and Fort Bend counties. While prospects for the Texas rice crop were considered good before the storm, the hurricane's wind and rain caused lingering uncertainty about yield and quality losses. Reports indicated that some rice fields were blown over, The early timing of the hurricane was a key factor, as most of the rice was still in a flooded state at the time. <2> Riceland Foods, a farmer-owned cooperative, announced the election of three new members to its board of directors. Curtis Fox of Gillett will represent the Stuttgart District, Britt Allmon of Pollard will serve the Northeast Arkansas District, and Cole Hicks of Walnut Ridge will represent the Jonesboro District. [1, 2, 5] The new members began their three-year terms in May 2024. [2, 5] The election was announced following the retirement of three former board members. [2] <3> BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, projected on April 12, 2024, that global rice prices are expected to stay elevated throughout 2024. The forecast attributes this to sustained market tightness resulting from unfavorable weather and ongoing export restrictions from India. Specifically, BMI anticipates that second-month rough rice futures on the Chicago Board of Trade will average US$16.50 per hundredweight (cwt) in 2024. <4> The World Bank forecasted that rice prices are expected to see a further increase of 6 percent in 2024; This prediction is based on the threat of El Niño; This prediction is based on policy responses from major rice exporters and importers <5> In late October 2023, an analysis of the U.S. rice export market revealed that prices for No. 2, 4% broken long grain milled rice had been holding steady at $760 per ton since late January 2023, marking the highest price for this rice variety since October 2008. Similarly, quotes for Latin American markets had also been stable at $725 per ton since late January. This period of price stability occurred while the global rice market was significantly impacted by India's decision to ban the export of non-basmati white rice in July 2023. India, the world's largest rice exporter, accounted for approximately 40% of the global rice trade in the 2022-2023 marketing year, and the ban affected about 15% of global rice trade. <6> In a report published on September 19, 2023, the USDA analyzed the global impact of India's rice export restrictions, which were projected to cause a decline in global rice trade for both 2023 and 2024. [6] India, the world's largest rice exporter, initiated these disruptions by banning non-basmati white rice exports on July 20, 2023, and subsequently imposing an export tax on parboiled rice in August 2023. [4, 6] These actions triggered a surge in global rice prices to their highest levels since 2008, as importers shifted demand to the next largest suppliers, Thailand and Vietnam. [2] The USDA report noted that U.S. rice exports were not expected to be significantly affected, as their prices were already substantially higher than the global average. [2] <7> On July 20, 2023, India, the world's largest rice exporter, announced an immediate ban on the export of non-basmati white rice. The measure, implemented by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade, was intended to control rising domestic prices and ensure domestic food security amid concerns of a potentially poor monsoon. This action, which amended the export policy for this rice category from "free" to "prohibited," immediately sparked concerns about the stability of global rice supplies and prices. <8> On June 28, 2023, Anheuser-Busch, the leading end-user of rice in the United States, launched a new advertising campaign titled "We Make the Beer" to coincide with the start of the summer season. The campaign's purpose is to recognize the various components of its business, including employees, branding, partnerships, and programming that contribute to their product. Featured in the campaign is Eric Vaught, a fourth-generation rice farmer from Hickory Ridge, Arkansas, who represents the many American farmers who supply the critical rice ingredient for the company's brewing process. This initiative underscores the significant role of the U.S. rice industry in Anheuser-Busch's products and the nation's economy. <9> A bipartisan group of U.S. Representatives, including Tracey Mann (R-KS), John Garamendi (D-CA), Rick Crawford (R-AR), and Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), introduced H.R. 4293, the 'American Farmers Feed the World Act of 2023'. [5, 6, 7] The legislation, introduced to the House on June 22, 2023, aims to amend the Food for Peace Act to ensure that U.S.-grown agricultural commodities are the primary component of international food aid. [1, 2, 7] Key provisions of the bill include prohibiting the use of cash transfers, food vouchers, and food procured internationally. [1, 2] It also mandates that at least 50% of the program's annual funding be used for the procurement and ocean transportation of American agricultural products, while reducing the allowable percentage for administrative expenses. [1, 9] The bill proposes to increase oversight for the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) by requiring more detailed reporting to Congress and transferring some authorities to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). [1, 3, 7] The proposed legislation has garnered support from over 55 agricultural and maritime organizations. [7, 9] <10> As Louisiana's 2023 rice crop neared summer, its progression towards harvest was aided by warmer temperatures and afternoon showers, according to LSU AgCenter rice specialist Ronnie Levy. The warm and wet weather conditions created a favorable environment for fungal diseases such as blast and cercospora, prompting growers to actively scout their fields. While some disease was beginning to appear, LSU AgCenter entomologist Blake Wilson reported that insect pressure had been minimal so far in the growing season.

Among the advancements discussed were the use of AI-driven systems for quality control, as exemplified by Gautam Rice, and the integration of blockchain technology to provide unprecedented supply chain transparency and ensure the authenticity of rice from farm to table. The analysis emphasized a clear shift in consumer behavior towards products that reflect environmental stewardship and ethical sourcing. <2> The potential for a large U.S. rice crop was questioned following extreme rains from Hurricane Beryl, which made landfall in Texas on July 8, 2024. The storm particularly impacted southern growing areas near Houston, including Wharton, Brazoria, Matagorda, Colorado, and Fort Bend counties. While prospects for the Texas rice crop were considered good before the storm, the hurricane's wind and rain caused lingering uncertainty about yield and quality losses. Reports indicated that some rice fields were blown over, and by early September, farmers confirmed that yields were down 15-18% compared to the previous year, an impact attributed to the storm hitting during the crucial pollination stage. The early timing of the hurricane was a key factor, as most of the rice was still in a flooded state at the time. <3> Riceland Foods, a farmer-owned cooperative, announced the election of three new members to its board of directors. Curtis Fox of Gillett will represent the Stuttgart District, Britt Allmon of Pollard will serve the Northeast Arkansas District, and Cole Hicks of Walnut Ridge will represent the Jonesboro District. [1, 2, 5] The new members began their three-year terms in May 2024. [2, 5] The election was announced following the retirement of three former board members. Specifically, BMI anticipates that second-month rough rice futures on the Chicago Board of Trade will average US$16.50 per hundredweight (cwt) in 2024. <5> The World Bank forecasted that rice prices are expected to see a further increase of 6 percent in 2024; This prediction is based on the threat of El Niño; This prediction is based on policy responses from major rice exporters and importers <6> In late October 2023, an analysis of the U.S. rice export market revealed that prices for No. 2, 4% broken long grain milled rice had been holding steady at $760 per ton since late January 2023, marking the highest price for this rice variety since October 2008. Similarly, quotes for Latin American markets had also been stable at $725 per ton since late January. This period of price stability occurred while the global rice market was significantly impacted by India's decision to ban the export of non-basmati white rice in July 2023. The measure, implemented by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade, was intended to control rising domestic prices and ensure domestic food security amid concerns of a potentially poor monsoon. This action, which amended the export policy for this rice category from "free" to "prohibited," immediately sparked concerns about the stability of global rice supplies and prices. <9> On June 28, 2023, Anheuser-Busch, the leading end-user of rice in the United States, launched a new advertising campaign titled "We Make the Beer" to coincide with the start of the summer season. The campaign's purpose is to recognize the various components of its business, including employees, branding, partnerships, and programming that contribute to their product. Featured in the campaign is Eric Vaught, a fourth-generation rice farmer from Hickory Ridge, Arkansas, who represents the many American farmers who supply the critical rice ingredient for the company's brewing process. This initiative underscores the significant role of the U.S. rice industry in Anheuser-Busch's products and the nation's economy. <10> A bipartisan group of U.S. Representatives, including Tracey Mann (R-KS), John Garamendi (D-CA), Rick Crawford (R-AR), and Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), introduced H.R. 4293, the 'American Farmers Feed the World Act of 2023'. [1, 2, 7] Key provisions of the bill include prohibiting the use of cash transfers, food vouchers, and food procured internationally. [1, 2] It also mandates that at least 50% of the program's annual funding be used for the procurement and ocean transportation of American agricultural products, while reducing the allowable percentage for administrative expenses. [1, 9] The bill proposes to increase oversight for the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) by requiring more detailed reporting to Congress and transferring some authorities to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). [1, 3, 7] The proposed legislation has garnered support from over 55 agricultural and maritime organizations. [7, 9]
